CLOSED_COMPS_ANALYSIS: Sixteen homes closed in The Point over the past year in the $2.25M–$5M range. The closed avg $/SF is $591 and the median is $556, with a 95% list-to-sale ratio and average DOM of 36 days. The premium waterfront tier — Milford Circle ($947/SF), Brawley School ($804/SF), Rehoboth Lane ($775/SF) — sold quickly. Non-waterfront closings ranged from $2.25M–$2.45M ($274–$564/SF), with 123 Stonewall Beach Lane ($274/SF) an outlier due to its large 8,640 SF depressing the $/SF figure. 105 Grey Lady Court ($3.675M, $502/SF, 19 DOM) is waterfront and sold cleanly at 94% of ask. For non-waterfront comparisons, the relevant closed range is $2.25M–$2.45M.

NWF_COMPS_ANALYSIS: The non-waterfront data tells the clearest story. Four non-waterfront homes closed in The Point over the past year — all between $2,250,000 and $2,449,000, with a median of $2,382,000 and avg $/SF of $455. The strongest comparable for 131 The Point is 167 Quaker Road — also golf course, non-waterfront, sold at $449/SF in 8 days at full ask. However, 131 The Point commands a meaningful premium over Quaker: full brick construction (vs. mixed), 6,178 SF (vs. 5,451 SF — 13% larger), a Simonini-built heated pebble-tec pool, and a deeded boat slip. Applying a conservative adjustment for size, brick, pool, and lake access: $449/SF + ~$50/SF premium = ~$499/SF — landing precisely at the recommended price of $2,990,000. This makes $2,990,000 the most defensible and data-supported price point for 131 The Point in the current market.
